title.narrative: Output 3.3. Increased capacity of Member States to formulate and implement policies for a just transition towards environmentally sustainable economies and societies

description.narrative:
The Federal Ministry of Finance, Budget and National Planning (MFBNP) in collaboration with the tripartite partners and other relevant stakeholders, mainstreamed over the years 2022-23, Just Transition into the Policy Implementation Plan, and Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Framework of the new National Social Protection Policy (NSPP). The Implementation Plan, and the M&E Framework were consequently adopted at a two-day validation workshop held in June 2023. The tripartite partners have earlier carried out a Feasibility Study on Enhancing Social Protection Coverage in Support for Just Transition in Nigeria. The study was carried out along two major axes as part of the partnerships with the French government (2020-2024), and the AFD (COPAR 2021). -With this development just transition indicators have been successfully integrated into the National Social Protection Policy (NSPP), Implementation Plan, and M&E Framework. This will also enhance extending social protection coverage to workers and their families in the informal and rural economy. -This is commandable for the ILO social dimension of the ecological transition, which is progressing in integrating social protection policies for workers as part of the ecological transition.
The findings of the Feasibility Study were essential to mainstreaming Just Transition into the Implementation Plan, and the M&E Framework of the NSSP. The adopted documents will be in use from 2023 to 2028. ILO supported the tripartite partners to execute the Feasibility Study. These includes - supporting various engagements and consultations for the study including the inception workshop which took place in March 2022. This gave the tripartite partners and other stakeholders the opportunity to assess the work plan and methodology of the study and contribute to effectively to the exécution of the study. -the ILO also provided technical backstopping to the study team, and also took part in the review of the study report. Hence, their contributions also enhanced the overall quality of the report.
Also, ILO supported the Federal Ministry of Finance, Budget and National Planning to organise a two-day validation workshop in June 2023, Mararaba, Nasarawa State, Nigeria. This also came with the engagement of two facilitators for the review and update of the Implementation Plan, and Monitoring and Evaluation Framework for the National Social Protection Policy.
